subject: KPI runway snapshot and QBR asks
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: KPI runway snapshot and QBR asks

Team —

Ahead of next week's leadership QBR I want a concise runway snapshot for the KPIs we care about: latency (p50/p95), cost per 1M tokens, uptime (7d rolling), and active usage (DAU/WAU for hosted API). The execs want:

- A one-slide summary of where each metric is relative to target + 3-week trend.
- Two scenario plans: a) optimistic (holiday traffic >+20%), b) conservative (model rollout regressions).
- Contingency actions tied to owners (e.g., fallback routing, temporary quantized variant, burst capacity triggers).

I've attached last month's dashboard export (nov-dashboard-v2.pdf) — it's our baseline. Specific asks:

1) Irene: validate latency regressions flagged on 11/18 and confirm whether kernel swap we rolled fixed p95 for RLHF workloads.
2) Laura: confirm cost delta from reserved vs. burst usage in US-EAST and give an overnight ops action for cost-limited mode.
3) Grace: confirm uptime story and list any customer-facing incidents we need to call out for the QBR.

Please reply with short bullets and owners by EOD Friday 12/1 so I can consolidate. If any of you need ACME input on usage patterns, I've CC'd their ops contact in a follow-up.

Thanks — Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference

Attachment: nov-dashboard-v2.pdf (PDF, 2.1MB)
From: Tamar Cohen <tamar.cohen@acme-analytics.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Nov 2028 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: KPI runway snapshot and QBR asks

Markus —

Quick note from Acme side: we saw a usage spike on 11/19 that looks correlated with our batch ingestion job; it pushed sustained 30% higher token volume for ~6 hours but latency held within p95 target because of your burst pool. We can share the ingestion schedule and throughput numbers if that helps the scenario planning.

Two small asks from our end for the QBR:
- Can you confirm the expected throttling policy under cost-limited mode (will it reject or queue requests)?
- If you surface an incident in the report, please include start/end times and whether KV-cache priming was affected.

Happy to jump on a 20-min sync if useful.

— Tamar
Ops Lead, Acme Analytics

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Nov 2028 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: KPI runway snapshot and QBR asks

Markus —

Notes against your asks:

- Latency: the 11/18 regression was traced to an inefficient attention kernel selection for the 8k-sequence RLHF variant. Kernel swap deployed 11/22 reduced p95 by ~18% for the sampled workload; p50 unchanged. I attached the quick test log and the qbr-contingency-playbook.docx with proposed rollback and hotfix steps.
- Scenario plans: optimistic (capacity absorb via burst + cache warmers), conservative (route RLHF to quantized variant + enable cost-limited graceful degrade). Both are documented in the playbook.

Action owners (short):
- Irene: validate prod can route RLHF->quantized variant automatically (in progress, ETA 12/2).
- Laura: finalize cost-limited policy text for the slide (need your confirmation on reject vs queue behavior).
- Grace: produce incident timeline for 11/19 spike and confirm customer impact (Grace to confirm by 12/1).

I'll be available for a quick run-through 12/1 10:00-10:30 PT if you want to walk the slide.

Irene Choi
Head of Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: qbr-contingency-playbook.docx (Word doc, 420KB)

Date: Fri, 1 Dec 2028 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: KPI runway snapshot and QBR asks

All —

Quick bullets from finance/ops angle:
- Cost delta: reserved capacity covered 62% of US-EAST demand in Nov; burst usage accounted for the rest. Net cost per 1M tokens rose 9% month-over-month due to three high-concurrency customer campaigns.
- Cost-limited mode behavior: default is graceful degrade (queue up to 2s) then reject; if leadership wants reject-first we can flip the policy but it increases customer-visible errors during spikes.

Action: I'll draft the one-slide cost note and mark the two policy options. ETA for slide text: EOD 12/1.

Laura Bennett
Director, Cost & Capacity Strategy
Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — solid updates. Consolidated next steps for the QBR slide deck (short):

1) Irene: confirm automated routing test completed and % reduction in p95 by 12/2 EOD. If not green, include rollback plan on the slide.
2) Laura: attach a single-line cost policy recommendation (queue->reject toggle) and the cost delta footnote, slide text by 12/1 EOD (received).
3) Grace: incident timeline and customer impact statement for 11/19 spike; if any impacted customers request remediation we will surface in the QBR notes.
4) Tamar/Acme: please share ingestion schedule (CSV) if possible — we'll include it in the appendix.

I will stitch the one-slide summary and send a final review copy to this thread by 12/4 09:00 PT. If anyone has anything that must be called out for the board-level deck, flag it now.

Appreciate the fast turn on this — Markus
